content.text: Read docs/session-three-brief.md first. It is committed in this repo and it is your spec for this session. Also read CODEBUDDY.md for the locked scope. Your job this session is the five items in that brief, in its priority order: F3 (notes leak into the party-facing card), F4 (ruled + null ruling claims a delivery that never happened), F5 (one null event kills the whole document), the policy.source_path absolute-path producer fix, and event 9's summary restating the withheld amount. Non-negotiable working rules for this session: 1. One item at a time. Verify each in a real browser against a real file under runs/ before you move to the next. Do not describe a fix as working; open it and look. 2. A fix is not done until a test FAILS when the fix is reverted. After each fix, write the pinning test, then reintroduce the defect, run the suite, and confirm RED. Then restore the fix and confirm GREEN. Report both results per item. A growing test count is not the acceptance criterion; the specific defect reproducing a failure is. 3. Items 4 and 5 are PRODUCER fixes. They belong in app/, not in ui/. Find where policy.source_path is set and where the event summaries are written before you change anything. Do not patch the symptom in the view. 4. ui/ and app/ are yours. tools/ and tests/ exist already with 178 passing tests; you may ADD tests, you may not weaken or edit an existing test to make something pass. 5. Commit after each verified item, with a message that says why the change was needed, not just what changed. 6. This repo is public. Never commit credentials, and never commit anything under runs/. 7. If any item in the brief conflicts with CODEBUDDY.md or with the statement extract in docs/, STOP and ask rather than guessing. Start by running the pre-flight in the brief, then plan the five items before writing code.

1→# Build session three — brief
   2→
   3→**Status at handoff: 2026-09-22, after session two.** Head `bc3d751`. Suite 178 tests, green.
   4→`ui/` now holds `index.html`, `app.js`, `styles.css`.
   5→
   6→Pre-flight:
   7→
   8→```bash
   9→cd ~/hermes-workspace/projects/ryde-build
  10→codebuddy --version          # the CLI self-updates; a bad update bricked it once
  11→git status --short           # expect empty
  12→python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .    # expect 178 tests, OK
  13→```
  14→
  15→---
  16→
  17→## What session two delivered, verified by execution
  18→
  19→Five commits (`537f899` → `ed061e1`) built the case-file view. Verified in a real browser by
  20→the planner lane, not by reading the model's summary:
  21→
  22→- All three outcomes render distinctly from real `case_file.json` files.
  23→- **No hardcoded case content.** `RD-0101`, `RD-0109`, `OS-0301`, `NS-0201`, `8.0347`, `25.54`,
  24→  `55.16`, `5.81` all absent from `ui/`.
  25→- **The central safety property holds.** On RD-0109 the party-facing region contains only the
  26→  neutral message. The Judge's confidence `0.86` appears nowhere outside the human-only region.
  27→  `renderWithheldResolution` never passes the resolution object to the party renderer.
  28→- XSS-safe by construction: zero `innerHTML`, all text through `textContent`.
  29→- Path traversal blocked in `normalizedPayloadRef` (rejects absolute, drive-letter, `..`, empty).
  30→- 178 tests still pass; `tools/` and `tests/` untouched.
  31→
  32→A glm-5.3 adversarial review then attacked it. Its headline verdict ("central safety claim
  33→false") was **not accepted**: it grepped for the string `55.16` and did not distinguish the
  34→*claimed* amount, which the rider wrote on the intake form and which is public by definition,
  35→from the *withheld ruling* amount. Those two are numerically identical in this fixture by
  36→coincidence. The Judge's confidence, which exists only in the ruling, does not leak.
  37→
  38→But the review found three real defects the author missed. All three were reproduced firsthand
  39→in a browser before being written down here.
  40→
  41→---
  42→
  43→## The work, in priority order
  44→
  45→### 1. F3 — `human_review` renders `resolution.notes` into the party-facing card (CRITICAL)
  46→
  47→`ui/app.js:599`. `renderHumanReviewResolution` calls `appendResolutionNotes(body,
  48→resolution.notes)`, and that card is marked `data-audience="parties"` at `app.js:589`.
  49→
  50→The same `notes` field is treated as human-only in the withheld path (`app.js:581`). One field,
  51→two different audience rulings, in one file. That inconsistency is the defect.
  52→
  53→It is not live today only because `human_review` cases skip the Judge, so their notes carry no
  54→ruling figures. But the producer does put ruling figures in notes: the shipped RD-0109 note
  55→reads `"the ruling was not delivered: SGD 55.16 exceeds the autonomous decision cap of SGD
  56→50.00"`. A future producer change, or a mislabelled outcome, leaks it straight to the parties.
  57→
  58→**Reproduced:** take `runs/…-OS-0301/case_file.json`, set
  59→`resolution.notes = ["INTERNAL: candidate refund SGD 55.16 at confidence 0.86"]`, load it.
  60→The string renders under NOTES inside the parties-marked card. Observed
  61→`PARTY_HAS_5516: true, PARTY_HAS_086: true`.
  62→
  63→**Fix direction:** `notes` is operator commentary in every outcome. Render it outside the
  64→party-facing card, consistently with the withheld path. Pin with a test that fails when the
  65→notes go back into the party region.
  66→
  67→### 2. F4 — `ruled` with a null `ruling` claims a delivery that never happened (MAJOR)
  68→
  69→`ui/app.js:545` writes the header "RULING ISSUED / The Judge delivered this decision to the
  70→parties" before `appendRulingDetails` early-returns on a null ruling (`app.js:519-521`).
  71→
  72→**Reproduced:** `runs/…-RD-0101/case_file.json` with `resolution.ruling = null` renders the
  73→delivery claim over an empty metrics grid, above the "still under review" party message. The
  74→card contradicts itself.
  75→
  76→This matters more than its severity label suggests. An observability tool that asserts a
  77→delivery which did not occur is the exact failure this project exists to prevent. Branch on the
  78→data, not on the outcome label alone: if `outcome` is `ruled` and `ruling` is null, that is a
  79→malformed case file and the view should say so plainly.
  80→
  81→### 3. F5 — one `null` element in `events` makes the whole case file unviewable (MAJOR)
  82→
  83→`ui/app.js:672` reads `event.seq` on null and throws. `handleFile` catches it (`app.js:732`),
  84→hides the entire workspace, and shows the raw JS message "Cannot read properties of null
  85→(reading 'seq')".
  86→
  87→**Reproduced.** One bad event should degrade that row, not the document.
  88→
  89→### 4. `policy.source_path` renders an absolute home-directory path (MINOR, but it is a producer fix)
  90→
  91→The Case metadata block shows
  92→`[USER_HOME]/hermes-workspace/projects/ryde-build/docs/policy.md`.
  93→
  94→`runs/` is gitignored so this never reaches the public repo, but it lands in every demo
  95→screenshot and in the video. **The fix belongs in the pipeline, not the view** — emit a path
  96→relative to the repo root. Check where `policy.source_path` is set before changing the view.
  97→
  98→### 5. Event 9's summary restates the withheld amount (JUDGEMENT CALL, not a defect)
  99→
 100→`runs/…-RD-0109` event 9 reads "Judge withheld the ruling: SGD 55.16 exceeds the autonomous
 101→decision cap of SGD 50.00".
 102→
 103→This page is the operator console; parties never see it, so this is not a leak. But the event
 104→strip carries no audience marking at all, and a reviewer reading the page cold called it one.
 105→Softening the summary to name the rule without restating the figure costs nothing and removes
 106→the argument. Producer-side change, in the events layer.
 107→
 108→---
 109→
 110→## What is NOT in this session
 111→
 112→**The Tencent endpoint (W3) is stalled, not skipped.** There is no API key yet. See the
 113→acquisition note below — it is a the operator task, not a build task, and the build cannot proceed past
 114→it.
 115→
 116→**The party-facing surface does not exist and is not in scope here.** `ui/` is the internal ops
 117→console. The locked scope (`CODEBUDDY.md:44-47`) has parties as spectators behind a
 118→standardized intake form, with a follow-up question path and an outcome message. None of that
 119→is built; disputes are read from `data/disputes/*.json` and nobody has ever typed into a form.
 120→That is a separate session, to be scoped after the defects are closed.
 121→
 122→---
 123→
 124→## Working rules (unchanged)
 125→
 126→- One capability at a time, verified in a browser before moving on.
 127→- **Verify by running it, not by describing it.**
 128→- `ui/` and `app/` are yours. `tools/` and `tests/` are not; do not modify tests to make
 129→  something pass.
 130→- **A fix is not done until a test fails when the fix is reverted.** Session one shipped a
 131→  judge-citation repair against a fully green 178-test suite because nothing exercised the bad
 132→  path. Each fix above needs a test that fails on reintroduction.
 133→- Commit after each verified step with a message explaining why, not just what.
 134→- The repo is PUBLIC. Never commit credentials.

1→# PROJECT: Ryde — Multi-Agent Autonomous Dispute Resolution
   2→
   3→**Status: BUILDING (2026-09-21).** Planning closed **2026-09-19** and the scope, stack and
   4→workflow are ruled. This file is CodeBuddy's memory for this project: the builder's entry
   5→point. The ruled scope lives in
   6→the planning repository and is deliberately unreadable from here (the permission fence in
   7→`.codebuddy/settings.json` denies reads of that path, and it is verified to work), so
   8→**everything you need is in this file, `docs/` and the kickoff prompt the operator gives you**.
   9→If a session needs a fact that is neither here nor in the docs: stop and ask; do not invent
  10→scope.
  11→
  12→## What this project is
  13→
  14→Ryde track entry for the Tencent Cloud "AI CAN DO IT" Hackathon Singapore 2026. The challenge is a
  15→**multi-agent autonomous dispute resolution system** for ride-hailing disputes: a Rider Advocate
  16→agent, a Driver Advocate agent, and a Judge agent that weighs both cases, applies company policy and
  17→issues a ruling with a confidence score.
  18→
  19→`docs/statement-extract.md` holds the challenge statement verbatim. Read it before any build work.
  20→It is the requirements floor: the locked scope below is the team's chosen subset of it, and the
  21→locked scope never widens past the statement.
  22→
  23→## Hard requirements (non-negotiable)
  24→
  25→- The project must be **original** and built on **at least one of CodeBuddy or WorkBuddy**.
  26→- **Proof of product usage is mandatory.** Without it the project is **not scored at all**. Evidence
  27→  is screenshots of CodeBuddy/WorkBuddy chat logs, minimum three, accumulated as work happens. It
  28→  cannot be reconstructed later, so capture as you go.
  29→- The project must be **demoable end to end for at least two dispute categories**.
  30→- **Inter-agent communication must be observable** to a judge: a visible log or UI showing how the
  31→  agents exchange information and build their cases.
  32→- Deliverables include a public GitHub repo with complete source, an architecture diagram, and a live
  33→  demo walkthrough.
  34→- The repository is **PUBLIC**. Never commit credentials, API keys, tokens or personal data.
  35→
  36→## Locked build scope
  37→
  38→These decisions are ruled by the team and are **not open to re-litigation**:
  39→
  40→- **Categories:** route deviation + no-show charge, end to end. No third category.
  41→- **Agents:** exactly three — Rider Advocate, Driver Advocate, Judge. The Judge always emits a
  42→  confidence score (0–1). Below a configurable threshold it does not rule; the parties see only
  43→  a neutral "your case is still under review" message. Escalation is MVP, not stretch.
  44→- **Parties are spectators:** disputes arrive through a standardized intake form (category
  45→  dropdown; "other" routes to a human-review queue with a neutral message). The advocates screen
  46→  the submitted answers and may ask the party targeted follow-ups only when data conflicts or
  47→  is insufficient. No fourth intake agent. Parties never chat with the agents.
  48→- **Deterministic evidence layer:** all quantitative evidence (route deviation km/%, duration vs
  49→  estimate, fare recomputation, cancellation timestamps, chat-log signals, behaviour profile)
  50→  is computed in Python into a typed **Evidence Pack**. Agents may cite pack fields; they must
  51→  never do the arithmetic themselves.
  52→- **Policy as a swappable document:** `docs/policy.md`, rules with IDs and machine-checkable
  53→  preconditions, provenance stated in the file. The Judge and advocates cite rule IDs. A real
  54→  organiser version, if one ever arrives, drops in with no code change.
  55→- **Dataset as a swappable document:** synthesised corpus in `data/`, labelled with
  56→  ground-truth rulings (the correct ruling per case, by design) so replayed-run consistency is
  57→  measurable. Same swap rule.
  58→- **Observability surface (required by the statement):** a case-file view — each side's claim,
  59→  evidence and policy citations, with agent-to-agent traffic as a compact timestamped event
  60→  strip (full text one click deeper). This screen is the demo's home.
  61→- **Stack:** Python backend + plain HTML/JS front end. No heavy framework. The backend calls
  62→  Tencent Cloud's LLM API directly (key in `.env`, never committed). CodeBuddy writes the code;
  63→  it is never the runtime.
  64→- **Repo layout:** `app/` (Python backend), `ui/` (front end), `docs/` (architecture diagram,
  65→  policy set, dataset description), `evidence/` (development-process screenshots), `tools/` +
  66→  `tests/` (marked **non-app**: helper scripts and tests only; `app/` and `ui/` never import
  67→  from them). **The repo is PUBLIC at submission — never commit credentials or personal data.**
  68→- **Deployment:** local run for the live demo (real backend, real LLM calls); a static replay
  69→  of one real case on EdgeOne Pages for the optional public link, labelled honestly as a replay.
  70→
  71→## Non-negotiable engineering rules
  72→
  73→- Never commit `.env`, API keys, tokens, or any credential. The repo is public.
  74→- Do not read or write anything outside this folder — **this is a rule you must honour, not
  75→  something the fence guarantees.** The permission fence in `.codebuddy/settings.json` denies
  76→  reads of the planning repository path and of secret files (`.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`,
  77→  `secrets/`), denies `curl`, `wget`, `rm -rf` and `git push`, and asks before `git remote`.
  78→  It does NOT block other writes or other reads. Staying inside this folder is your job.
  79→- Verify work by running it, not by describing it. A feature is done when it has been exercised and
  80→  the real output checked.
  81→- Keep the demo path working at all times. A half-built stretch goal that breaks the main flow is
  82→  worse than no stretch goal.
  83→- **Only the CodeBuddy build lane writes `app/` and `ui/`.** Any other AI assistant used for
  84→  rescue or unblocking (e.g. another coding agent) is confined to `tools/` and `tests/` and must never
  85→  touch application code — the project's "built on CodeBuddy" claim must stay honest.
  86→
  87→## How work is done here
  88→
  89→- **One capability at a time**, verified before moving on.
  90→- Commit with a clear message after each verified step.
  91→- Log decisions as they are made. A future session starts from these files, not from memory.
  92→- **Effort follows the Demo Day rubric:** 40 of 100 points are story, design and presentation,
  93→  so `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and the demo walkthrough are deliverables on the same
  94→  footing as code — polished after the MVP floor is standing, never skipped.
  95→- **Run from this folder.** `cd ~/hermes-workspace/projects/ryde-build && codebuddy`. Sessions are
  96→  scoped by launch directory, and this folder carries its own memory file and permission fence.
  97→- **Default model is `deepseek-v4.1-flash`** (global default, x0.00 cost multiplier). Override per
  98→  task with `--model <id>` only when the work warrants the expense: GPT-5.6-Luna x0.14 is the cheap
  99→  upgrade, Kimi-K3 x1.62 for hard reasoning. Never use Primary, Deep, Sol or GPT-6-Astra here.
 100→- **Headless capture:** `codebuddy -p "<prompt>" --output-format json` returns machine-readable
 101→  results and writes a transcript to `~/.codebuddy/projects/`. Useful when the build needs to be
 102→  driven from outside the interactive session.
 103→
 104→## Layout
 105→
 106→```
 107→ryde-build/
 108→├── CODEBUDDY.md            # this file — project memory + locked scope
 109→├── README.md               # judge's entry point (judge-first: what it is → see it run → diagram)
 110→├── .codebuddy/
 111→│   ├── settings.json       # permission fence
 112→│   └── rules/              # topic-scoped rules (added as the build needs them)
 113→├── app/                    # Python backend — agents, evidence layer, LLM calls
 114→├── ui/                     # plain HTML/JS front end — case-file observability view (to come)
 115→├── data/                   # synthesised dispute corpus, ground-truth labelled (17 cases; swappable)
 116→├── docs/
 117→│   ├── statement-extract.md  # challenge statement, verbatim — the only requirements source
 118→│   ├── policy.md             # policy rule set (32 rules; swappable; provenance stated in-file)
 119→│   ├── dataset.md            # dataset description + provenance
 120→│   ├── architecture.md       # required deliverable: diagram + system description (to come)
 121→│   └── evidence-plan.md      # §8 evidence rules and naming
 122→├── evidence/               # §8 screenshots (YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<topic>.png|.jpg)
 123→├── tools/                  # NON-APP helper scripts — app/ never imports from here
 124→└── tests/                  # NON-APP tests (178, stdlib only)
 125→```
 126→
 127→Files marked "(to come)" are authored in their own build sessions; do not create them as a
 128→side effect of other work.
 129→

## Smallest test seams for pinning each defect

`app.js` is a single IIFE (line 1 `(function () {`, line 752 `}());`) with **no exports and no module guard**. Everything is closure-private. At load time it only calls `document.getElementById` for 13 IDs and `addEventListener` on 2 of them (`picker` at 745, `runFolderPicker` at 749) — no rendering happens until a `change` event fires.

### Seam A — Node + minimal DOM stub, no dependencies (recommended)

`vm.runInNewContext(fs.readFileSync("ui/app.js", "utf8"), sandbox)` with a `sandbox.document` implementing `getElementById` and `createElement`. The stub's `addEventListener` captures the `change` handler, so the test can drive the real `handleFile` → `renderCase` path by setting `picker.files = [fakeFile]` with `fakeFile.text()` returning `Promise.resolve(JSON.stringify(caseFile))`.

Required stub surface: `className`, `textContent`, `dataset`, `classList.add`, `appendChild`, `removeChild`, `firstChild`, `addEventListener`, `hidden`, `id`, `href`, `title`, `open`, `files`, plus `text()` on the fake File. Roughly 80 lines of plain JS — no `npm install`, so it does not breach the stdlib-only toolchain constraint.

Then the assertion is a tree walk, not a string grep — which is what makes it a real pin rather than the grep that produced the rejected glm-5.3 review:

- **F3:** walk `#resolution-content`; collect `textContent` of every node whose nearest `[data-audience="parties"]` ancestor exists; assert `"55.16"` and `"0.86"` absent. Feed it `runs/20260922T110936Z-OS-0301/case_file.json` with `resolution.notes` set in the **in-memory copy** to `["INTERNAL: candidate refund SGD 55.16 at confidence 0.86"]` — exactly the brief's reproduction. Also assert the same for `#evidence-content` to catch lines 320–323.
- **F4:** `runs/20260922T114030Z-RD-0101/case_file.json` with `resolution.ruling = null` in memory. Assert the parties region does **not** contain `"delivered this decision"` and does contain a plain malformed-file statement.
- **F5:** `runs/20260922T114030Z-RD-0101/case_file.json` with `events = [events[0], null, events[1]]`. Assert `workspace.hidden === false`, that 2 event rows rendered, and that `status.textContent` is not `"Cannot read properties of null (reading 'seq')"`.

### Seam B — Python source-structure assertion (cheap supplement, weak)

A stdlib-only test that reads `ui/app.js` as text and asserts `appendResolutionNotes(` does not appear between the `dataset.audience = "parties"` line and the end of `renderHumanReviewResolution`. Fails on reintroduction and needs no Node, but tests source *text*, not behavior — it would pass if the function were reorganised while still leaking. Use only alongside Seam A, never instead of it.

### Seam C — extract an audience-policy table (structural fix, larger)

Give `app.js` a pure `resolutionAudienceSections(resolution)` returning `{party: [...], humanOnly: [...]}`, plus a one-line `if (typeof module !== "undefined") module.exports = {...}` guard so a Node test can call it with **no DOM stub at all**. This converts the safety property from "which parent did the author pass" into data that can be asserted directly, and it is the only option that makes F3 structurally impossible rather than merely fixed. It is larger than the brief's stated "fix direction" and would be a design decision to confirm.

**Note on placement:** the brief's working rules say `tools/` and `tests/` are "not yours; do not modify tests to make something pass" — yet it also requires "a test that fails when the fix is reverted." The consistent reading is: **add new test files, never edit existing ones to make them pass.** Worth confirming before implementation.

  63→|Driver Advocate Agent|Represents the driver's perspective|Gathers driver-side evidence, articulates the driver's defense based on policy, and argues for driver-favorable outcomes.|
  64→|Judge Agent|Acts as the impartial arbitrator|Weighs evidence from both advocates, applies company policy, issues a final ruling (refund, compensation, no action), and generates a natural language explanation of its reasoning.|
  65→
  66→##### MVP Evidence Sources (Text & Structured Data):
  67→
  68→- **GPS & Telemetry Data** — Route deviation analysis (comparing actual route vs. optimal route as data points), unexpected stops, trip duration vs. estimated time
  69→- **Chat & Communication Logs** — Text analysis for sentiment, agreements, disagreements, and threats
  70→- **Payment & Fare Data** — Fare breakdown validation, surge pricing disputes, promo code usage
  71→- **Historical Behavior Profiles** — Rider and driver dispute history, rating patterns, account age **MVP Workflow:**
  72→- A dispute is filed (e.g., "The driver took a longer route and I was overcharged.")
  73→- The Rider Advocate Agent and Driver Advocate Agent autonomously gather their respective evidence from the available data sources.
  74→- Each advocate builds and presents its case, citing relevant company policy.
  75→- The Judge Agent reviews both cases, applies policy, and issues a ruling with a confidence score and natural language reasoning summary.
  76→- The system outputs the ruling, recommended action (e.g., partial refund of $3.25), and explanation to both parties.

1→"""End-to-end orchestration for one dispute.
   2→
   3→The flow, and the traffic it leaves in the event log:
   4→
   5→    parties  -> system           dispute filed (the intake-form submission)
   6→    system   -> human_review     only for a category outside the two locked ones
   7→    system   -> agents           Evidence Pack built (deterministic, before any LLM call)
   8→    system   -> each advocate    case assigned
   9→    advocate -> judge            case submitted
  10→    advocate -> party            follow-up questions, only when the form is insufficient
  11→    system   -> judge            deliberation started, with both cases
  12→    judge    -> parties          ruling issued, or ruling withheld behind the gate
  13→    system   -> parties          the message the parties actually receive
  14→    system   -> system           run completed
  15→
  16→Nothing here decides anything: the evidence layer computes, the agents argue and rule,
  17→and this module only moves the case between them and records what happened.

  50→    dispute_id: str
  51→    category: str
  52→    generated_at: str

  81→    def write(self, run_dir: Path) -> Path:

 209→    case_file = CaseFile(

 327→class MatchingAnchorProvenanceTest(unittest.TestCase):
 328→    """Booking time is not matching time, and the pack must not conflate them.
 329→
 330→    NS-1's free window is 3 minutes wide and runs from matching. Booking happens first,
 331→    so measuring from booking overstates the interval and can deny a rider a free
 332→    cancellation they were entitled to. The substitution is allowed, but never silent.
 333→    """

 335→    def _pack_with(self, **changes):
 336→        record = json.loads((CORPUS / "NS-0206.json").read_text())
 337→        for key, value in changes.items():
 338→            if value is _ABSENT:
 339→                record["cancellation"].pop(key, None)
 340→            else:
 341→                record["cancellation"][key] = value
 342→        from app.dispute import parse_dispute
 343→
 344→        return build_evidence_pack(parse_dispute(record)).to_dict()

 346→    def test_the_anchor_actually_used_is_named(self):

 349→        self.assertIsNotNone(cancellation["matching_anchor_at"])

## 1. Test strategy — the decision that shapes everything

### Option A (recommended): Python stdlib structural invariants in a new `tests/test_ui_contract.py`

`ui/app.js` is one IIFE with no exports and no DOM; there is no JS engine in the Python stdlib, so a behavioural test is impossible without Node. Structural invariants run inside the existing `unittest` suite, add zero dependencies, and satisfy the brief's actual bar ("a test that fails when the fix is reverted").

The extractor is reliable on this file: **every top-level function sits at exactly 2-space indent** (`grep -n "^  function "` → 40 functions, lines 34-713), no inline callback begins a line with `  function `, and the IIFE closes with `\n}());` at `:752`. So:

```python
def _function_body(source, name):
    marker = "\n  function %s(" % name
    start = source.find(marker)
    if start == -1:
        raise AssertionError("no function %s in ui/app.js" % name)   # missing fix -> RED
    rest = source[start + 1:]
    ends = [p for p in (rest.find("\n  function ", 1), rest.find("\n}());")) if p != -1]
    return rest[:min(ends)] if ends else rest
```

The invariants below are **whole-file / ordering rules**, not copies of the fix lines, and each is RED on today's code (I traced them against the current source):

**F3 — `HumanReviewNotesAudienceTest`**
1. `test_resolution_notes_are_only_touched_by_human_only_paths`: for every function whose body contains `resolution.notes`, assert its body also contains `human-review-only`. Today offenders = `renderEvidence`, `renderHumanReviewResolution` → RED. After the fix the only two holders are `renderWithheldResolution` and `renderHumanReviewResolution`, both containing the marker.
2. `test_the_human_review_path_renders_the_notes_exactly_once`: `body.count("resolution.notes") == 1` in `renderHumanReviewResolution`. Today: 1 — but paired with (1) it closes the "partial revert" hole (party card **and** human card both rendering notes → count 2 → RED).

**F4 — `MalformedRuledResolutionTest`**
3. `test_the_delivery_claim_is_only_reachable_behind_a_ruling_guard`: in `renderRuledResolution`, `"delivered this decision"` must be present, a `typeof` guard must be present, `guard < claim`, and `"resolution.ruling"` must appear before the claim.
4. `test_a_malformed_ruled_file_is_named_and_not_party_facing`: `_function_body(SOURCE, "renderMalformedRuledResolution")` (absent today → AssertionError → RED) contains `MALFORMED` and does **not** contain `dataset.audience = "parties"`.

**F5 — `NullEventRowTest`**
5. `test_each_event_row_is_guarded_before_it_is_read`: in `renderEvents`, a guard (`typeof event` or `!event`) exists and precedes the first `event.seq`; body also contains `event-malformed`. Today no guard → RED.

**Honest limitation to state in the plan file:** these pins catch the reverted defect and the obvious re-break; they are not semantic execution. The browser check (mandatory per item) is the behavioural verification. If the user wants behaviour pins in CI, the only path is Option B and it costs the stdlib-only property.

### Option B (considered, not recommended): minimal Node DOM harness
Read `ui/app.js`, inject `globalThis.__ryde = {renderCase: …};` before the final `}());`, run in `vm` with a hand-rolled fake DOM (`createElement/getElementById/appendChild/removeChild/firstChild/textContent/classList/dataset/addEventListener`), call `renderCase` on synthetic case-file objects, walk the tree. ~250-300 lines, no npm packages. **Rejected because:** it requires the node binary (tests must `skipUnless(shutil.which("node"))`, so the pin silently disappears on machines without node — exactly the hole session one shipped), it contradicts `CODEBUDDY.md`'s "tests (178, stdlib only)" and the `python3 -m unittest discover` entry point, and the source transformation is brittle to the IIFE's closing token. Worth revisiting only if the user explicitly wants behavioural pins.

#: Repo root. The case file is screenshotted and shown in the demo video, so an absolute
#: path would put the builder's home directory on screen. A policy dropped in from outside

_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

Base directory for this skill: [USER_HOME]/.codebuddy/plugins/cache/codebuddy-plugins-official/agent-browser/1.3.0
# Agent Browser

Use `agent-browser` CLI for full browser automation tasks. It is suitable when a page needs JavaScript rendering, real browser interaction, screenshots, or form automation.

Upstream project: https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-browser

## Platform Support

`vercel-labs/agent-browser` provides native builds for:

- macOS ARM64 / x64
- Linux ARM64 / x64
- Windows x64

Windows support in this skill targets Windows 11 x64 with PowerShell and Node.js 18+.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+
- npm available in PATH
- Network access to install `agent-browser` and download Chromium
- About 500 MB free disk space for Chromium
- **The `node` binary on PATH must actually execute code**, not just print a version. `agent-browser` spawns a Node child process internally; if that Node is broken, the daemon will crash with no useful output even when `agent-browser --version` works.

  Quick check:
  ```bash
  node -e "console.log('ok')"
  ```
  If this does not print `ok` (SIGILL / exit 133 / any crash), the Node on PATH is unusable. Fix it, or run `agent-browser` with a known-good Node prepended to PATH for that command only:
  ```bash
  PATH="/path/to/working-node/bin:$PATH" agent-browser open <url>
  ```
  Inspect which Node would be picked up with `which -a node`.

## Installation

> Inside the CodeBuddy marketplace, `scripts/setup.sh` auto-runs these steps on first load. The commands below are for manual setup or reinstall.

### Windows PowerShell

```powershell
npm install -g agent-browser
agent-browser install
```

### macOS / Linux

```bash
npm install -g agent-browser
agent-browser install
```

### Linux missing dependencies

```bash
agent-browser install --with-deps
```

## Required Command Sequence

The current upstream `agent-browser` CLI does not require a separate `launch` command. `agent-browser open <url>` starts or connects to the browser daemon automatically.

Always follow this order:

1. Open target URL.
2. Wait for page load when needed.
3. Inspect page with `snapshot` or `snapshot -i`.
4. Interact with the page.
5. Close browser when done.

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot
agent-browser close
```

## Session Model

`agent-browser` runs a persistent background daemon. Understand this before planning multi-step tasks:

- The first `agent-browser open` starts a daemon; subsequent commands auto-connect to the same daemon.
- Within one session, cookies, localStorage and login state are preserved across commands.
- Multiple `open` calls in the same session navigate the existing browser (no need to close between URLs).
- `agent-browser close` ends the daemon. Only call it when the whole task is finished, not between steps of the same task.

Implication: for a task that visits N URLs, do **one** `open ... snapshot ...` chain per URL and **one** `close` at the very end, not N `open`/`close` pairs.

## Execution Principles

Apply these when running command sequences, especially in multi-step tasks:

- **`close` is mandatory in finally**: whether the task succeeds or fails midway, always run `agent-browser close` at the end to avoid zombie daemons and leaked Chromium processes.
- **`wait` is optional and degradable**: `wait --load networkidle` can hang on SPAs that never go idle. If a wait stalls, fall back to `wait --load load` or skip waiting and `snapshot` directly. Do not block the whole task on `wait`.
- **Reuse the daemon**: in the same task, do not `close` between intermediate steps. Open once, navigate/interact multiple times, close at the end.
- **Prefer `snapshot -i` for interaction**: when you need to click or type, get interactive element IDs first via `snapshot -i`, then act on them. Do not guess CSS selectors blindly.
- **Use agent-browser's own install channel**: for Chromium, runtime, or dependency issues, stay inside agent-browser's own tooling — `agent-browser install`, or the `playwright-core` CLI bundled under `$(npm root -g)/agent-browser/node_modules/playwright-core`. Do not run `npx playwright install` in parallel; it can fetch a revision that does not match what agent-browser expects and may time out downloading browsers agent-browser never uses.
- **Fail fast on environment errors**: if the very first `open` fails with daemon / Chromium / SIGILL errors, do not retry the same command repeatedly. Verify the Prerequisite Node check, then consult `references/troubleshooting.md`.

## When NOT to Use

`agent-browser` launches a real Chromium and consumes hundreds of MB plus a few seconds of cold start. Pick the lighter tool whenever possible:

| Need | Recommended tool |
|------|------------------|
| Fetch static HTML, plain text, or markdown of a page | WebFetch |
| Call a JSON / REST API | curl, fetch, or HTTP client |
| Read content already present in raw HTML | WebFetch |
| Render JavaScript-driven pages before reading | agent-browser |
| Click, type, login, or any multi-step interaction | agent-browser |
| Take a visual screenshot for review | agent-browser |
| Reproduce a real user flow end-to-end | agent-browser |

Rule of thumb: if `curl <url>` already contains the target content in plain HTML, do not start `agent-browser`.

## Essential Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `agent-browser open <url>` | Start or connect to the browser daemon and navigate to a URL. |
| `agent-browser wait --load networkidle` | Wait until network activity is idle. Useful after opening dynamic pages. |
| `agent-browser snapshot` | Get page content as text. |
| `agent-browser snapshot -i` | Get page content with element IDs for interaction. |
| `agent-browser screenshot` | Take a screenshot. |
| `agent-browser click <selector>` | Click an element. |
| `agent-browser type <selector> <text>` | Type text into an input. |
| `agent-browser close` | Close browser and free resources. |

## Common Workflows

### View webpage content

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot
agent-browser close
```

### Take screenshot

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser screenshot
agent-browser close
```

### Fill form and submit

First get interactive element IDs:

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com/login
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot -i
```

Then interact with stable selectors or element IDs:

```bash
agent-browser type "#username" "myuser"
agent-browser type "#password" "mypassword"
agent-browser click "#submit"
agent-browser close
```

### Extract data from a JavaScript-rendered page

```bash
agent-browser open https://example.com/data
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot
agent-browser close
```

## Windows Notes

On Windows, prefer PowerShell for installation and verification:

```powershell
npm install -g agent-browser
agent-browser install
agent-browser open https://example.com
agent-browser wait --load networkidle
agent-browser snapshot
agent-browser close
```

If the command is not found after installation, restart PowerShell or confirm npm global bin is in PATH:

```powershell
npm config get prefix
```

## Troubleshooting

For environment problems (daemon won't start, Chromium revision mismatch, SIGILL / Exit 133, install timeouts, etc.), see [`references/troubleshooting.md`](./references/troubleshooting.md). It is organized by symptom so you can diagnose against the actual error message instead of following a fixed script.

Quick checks before going there:

- `agent-browser` not found after install: restart shell, confirm npm global bin is in PATH (`npm config get prefix`).
- Linux browser launch missing system libs: `agent-browser install --with-deps`.
- Always run `agent-browser close` when a task ends, even on failure paths.

The UI displays this value verbatim.  The old pipeline serialized the resolved
absolute path, putting the builder's home directory into every demo artifact.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from app.dispute import load_dispute
from app.events import EventLog
from app.llm.mock import MockLLMClient
from app.pipeline import run_dispute
from app.policy import load_policy

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CORPUS = REPO / "data" / "disputes"


class PolicySourcePathTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def _run(self, dispute_id: str, policy_path: Path, tmp: Path):
        return run_dispute(
            dispute=load_dispute(CORPUS / (dispute_id + ".json")),
            llm=MockLLMClient(),
            policy=load_policy(policy_path),
            events=EventLog(tmp / "run", "policy-path-test"),
            confidence_threshold=0.65,
        )

    def test_repo_policy_is_emitted_relative_to_repo_root_everywhere(self):
        """The browser should show docs/policy.md, not the builder's home directory."""
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            tmp = Path(directory)
            case = self._run("RD-0101", REPO / "docs" / "policy.md", tmp)
            data = case.to_dict()
            self.assertEqual("docs/policy.md", data["policy"]["source_path"])
            self.assertEqual("docs/policy.md", case.policy_path)

            started = next(event for event in data["events"] if event["type"] == "run.started")
            payload = json.loads((tmp / "run" / started["payload_ref"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertEqual("docs/policy.md", payload["policy_path"])

    def test_human_review_case_uses_the_same_relative_policy_path(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            tmp = Path(directory)
            case = self._run("OS-0301", REPO / "docs" / "policy.md", tmp)
            self.assertEqual("docs/policy.md", case.to_dict()["policy"]["source_path"])

    def test_external_policy_does_not_emit_an_absolute_path(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            tmp = Path(directory)
            external_policy = tmp / "policy.md"
            external_policy.write_text(
                (REPO / "docs" / "policy.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                encoding="utf-8",
            )
            case = self._run("OS-0301", external_policy, tmp)
            source_path = case.to_dict()["policy"]["source_path"]
            self.assertEqual("policy.md", source_path)
            self.assertFalse(Path(source_path).is_absolute())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
"}

1→"""Command-line entry point.
   2→
   3→    python -m app.cli --dispute tests/fixtures/dispute_route_deviation.json
   4→    python -m app.cli --dispute <path> --policy docs/policy.md --llm tencent
   5→
   6→Runs one dispute through the full pipeline and writes the run's artifacts:
   7→
   8→    <out>/<run_id>/events.jsonl      append-only event log (the observable traffic)
   9→    <out>/<run_id>/payloads/*.json   full payload for each event
  10→    <out>/<run_id>/case_file.json    assembled record: evidence, claims, resolution, strip
  11→
  12→Defaults come from app/config.json; the flags override them for a single run.
  13→"""
  14→
  15→from __future__ import annotations
  16→
  17→import argparse
  18→import re
  19→import sys
  20→from datetime import datetime, timezone
  21→from pathlib import Path
  22→from typing import Optional, Sequence
  23→
  24→from .config import ConfigError, load_config
  25→from .dispute import DisputeError, load_dispute
  26→from .events import EventLog
  27→from .llm import LLMError, build_llm_client
  28→from .pipeline import run_dispute
  29→from .policy import PolicyError, load_policy
  30→
  31→EXIT_OK = 0
  32→EXIT_FAILED = 1
  33→
  34→
  35→def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
  36→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
  37→        prog="python -m app.cli",
  38→        description="Run one ride-hailing dispute through the multi-agent resolution pipeline.",
  39→    )
  40→    parser.add_argument("--dispute", required=True, help="path to one dispute JSON file")
  41→    parser.add_argument(
  42→        "--policy", default=None, help="path to the policy document (default: app/config.json)"
  43→    )
  44→    parser.add_argument(
  45→        "--llm",
  46→        default=None,
  47→        choices=["mock", "tencent"],
  48→        help="LLM provider (default: app/config.json). 'mock' needs no API key.",
  49→    )
  50→    parser.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="output directory for run artifacts")
  51→    parser.add_argument("--run-id", default=None, help="override the generated run id")
  52→    return parser
  53→
  54→
  55→def _slug(value: str) -> str:
  56→    return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "-", value).strip("-") or "run"
  57→
  58→
  59→def main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int:
  60→    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
  61→
  62→    try:
  63→        config = load_config()
  64→        dispute = load_dispute(Path(args.dispute))
  65→        policy = load_policy(Path(args.policy) if args.policy else config.policy_path)
  66→        provider = args.llm or config.llm.provider
  67→        llm = (
  68→            build_llm_client(provider, settings=config.llm)
  69→            if provider == "tencent"
  70→            else build_llm_client(provider)
  71→        )
  72→    except (ConfigError, DisputeError, PolicyError, LLMError) as exc:
  73→        print("error: %s" % exc, file=sys.stderr)
  74→        return EXIT_FAILED
  75→
  76→    out_dir = Path(args.out) if args.out else config.out_dir
  77→    run_id = args.run_id or "%s-%s" % (
  78→        datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ"),
  79→        _slug(dispute.dispute_id),
  80→    )
  81→    run_dir = out_dir / run_id
  82→    events = EventLog(run_dir, run_id)
  83→
  84→    try:
  85→        case_file = run_dispute(
  86→            dispute=dispute,
  87→            llm=llm,
  88→            policy=policy,
  89→            events=events,
  90→            confidence_threshold=config.confidence_threshold,
  91→            autonomous_cap_sgd=config.autonomous_cap_sgd,
  92→        )
  93→    except (DisputeError, PolicyError, LLMError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as exc:
  94→        print("error: the run failed: %s" % exc, file=sys.stderr)
  95→        print("partial event log: %s" % events.events_path, file=sys.stderr)
  96→        return EXIT_FAILED
  97→
  98→    case_path = case_file.write(run_dir)
  99→    _print_report(case_file, events, case_path)
 100→    return EXIT_OK
 101→
 102→
 103→def _print_report(case_file, events: EventLog, case_path: Path) -> None:
 104→    resolution = case_file.resolution
 105→    print("")
 106→    print("RYDE DISPUTE RESOLUTION — %s (%s)" % (case_file.dispute_id, case_file.category))
 107→    print("run: %s   llm: %s   threshold: %.2f"
 108→          % (case_file.run_id, resolution["ruling"]["llm"]["provider"] if resolution["ruling"] else "n/a",
 109→             case_file.confidence_threshold))
 110→    print("")
 111→    print("EVENT STRIP")
 112→    for event in events.snapshot():
 113→        print(
 114→            "%3d  %-24s %-18s -> %-16s %s"
 115→            % (event["seq"], event["ts"], event["from"], event["to"], event["summary"])
 116→        )
 117→    print("")
 118→    print("RESOLUTION")
 119→    print("  outcome:  %s" % resolution["outcome"])
 120→    if resolution["ruling"]:
 121→        ruling = resolution["ruling"]
 122→        print("  ruling:   %s of SGD %.2f (confidence %.2f)"
 123→              % (ruling["action"], ruling["recommended_amount_sgd"], ruling["confidence"]))
 124→        print("  rules:    %s" % (", ".join(ruling["cited_rule_ids"]) or "(none cited)"))
 125→    if resolution["withheld_candidate"]:
 126→        candidate = resolution["withheld_candidate"]
 127→        print("  withheld: %s of SGD %.2f at confidence %.2f — not delivered to the parties"
 128→              % (candidate["action"], candidate["recommended_amount_sgd"], candidate["confidence"]))
 129→    print("  parties:  %s" % resolution["party_message"])
 130→    print("")
 131→    print("ARTIFACTS")
 132→    print("  event log: %s" % events.events_path)
 133→    print("  case file: %s" % case_path)
 134→    print("")
 135→
 136→
 137→if __name__ == "__main__":
 138→    sys.exit(main())

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from app.dispute import load_dispute
from app.events import EventLog
from app.llm.mock import MockLLMClient
from app.pipeline import run_dispute
from app.policy import load_policy

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


class WithheldSummaryTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_withheld_event_names_the_gate_without_repeating_amounts(self):
        """The old event summary repeated both the candidate and cap amounts.

        The structured payload and reviewer notes remain the audit trail for figures;
        the compact event strip should explain the gate without restating them.
        """
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            tmp = Path(directory)
            case = run_dispute(
                dispute=load_dispute(REPO / "data" / "disputes" / "RD-0109.json"),
                llm=MockLLMClient(),
                policy=load_policy(REPO / "docs" / "policy.md"),
                events=EventLog(tmp / "run", "withheld-summary-test"),
                confidence_threshold=0.65,
                autonomous_cap_sgd=50.00,
            )
            data = case.to_dict()
            event = next(
                event for event in data["events"] if event["type"] == "judge.ruling_withheld"
            )
            summary = event["summary"]
            self.assertIn("cap", summary.lower())
            self.assertIn("ESC-4", summary)
            self.assertNotIn("SGD", summary)
            self.assertNotIn("55.16", summary)
            self.assertNotIn("50.00", summary)

            payload = json.loads((tmp / "run" / event["payload_ref"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertEqual(["ESC-4"], payload["gates_failed"])
            self.assertEqual(50.00, payload["autonomous_cap_sgd"])
            self.assertEqual(55.16, payload["withheld_candidate"]["recommended_amount_sgd"])
            self.assertIn("SGD 55.16", " ".join(data["resolution"]["notes"]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
"}

Two review rounds ran over your five commits. All five fixes were confirmed working and all five pinning tests were confirmed to go RED when reverted. Good work. ITEM 1 (MAJOR, this is the same defect class F4 claimed to fix): the F4 guard is shape-incomplete. ui/app.js renderRuledResolution checks `if (!resolution.ruling || typeof resolution.ruling !== "object")`. An empty array [], a non-empty array [1,2], and an empty object {} all pass that check, because typeof [] === "object" and [] is truthy. Only null, false, 0 and strings currently reach the MALFORMED card. A ruling object must be a non-array object carrying the fields the card claims to display; anything else is a malformed case file. Your pin test only covers ruling=null, which is why the suite stayed green. Extend the guard and extend the pin to cover [], {} and [1,2]. ITEM 2 (MINOR): the ruled path hardcodes "The Judge delivered this decision to the parties" and ignores resolution.delivered_to_parties. Reproduced: a ruled case with delivered_to_parties=false still asserts the delivery, and the flag is not displayed anywhere on that card. The withheld path does display the flag. Make the ruled card honest about a contradictory flag and display it, consistently with the withheld path. ITEM 3 (MINOR): Resolution.notes render nowhere on the ruled path. renderRuledResolution never calls appendResolutionNotes. The schema permits notes on any outcome, and you already ruled that notes are operator commentary in every outcome, so a ruled case carrying notes silently loses them. Render them in a human-only card on the ruled path too, exactly as you did for withheld and human_review. ITEM 4 (MINOR): app/pipeline.py _policy_source_path depends on the process working directory when source_path is relative. Reproduced: the same input 'docs/policy.md' returns 'docs/policy.md' when run from the repo and 'policy.md' when run from anywhere else, because Path.resolve() anchors to CWD. Anchor it to the repo root instead so the output is identical regardless of where the CLI was invoked, and pin that with a test that runs it from a different working directory. ITEM 5 (MINOR): tests/test_ui_contract.py _case_file_path prefers the newest artifact in runs/ over generating a fresh one. runs/ is untracked local state, so the pin can exercise stale data produced by pre-fix code, and the hardcoded assertions of 11/10/1 event rows break if a local run has a different event count. Always generate the fixture fresh from the corpus so the test means the same thing locally and on a clean checkout. name: Browser verification needs a no-store server
description: Chromium caches ui/app.js behind python -m http.server, so browser checks can silently test a pre-fix script; serve ui/ with Cache-Control no-store instead
type: project
---

Browser checks of `ui/` must be served with `Cache-Control: no-store`. `python3 -m
http.server` sends no cache headers, so Chromium keeps serving the previously loaded
`ui/app.js` even after a page reload — a fixed defect kept reproducing as if unfixed.

**Why:** during session four (2026-09-22) the ruling-shape guard looked ineffective in
the browser for several checks; `fetch("app.js")` from the page returned the old byte
length while the server was already serving the new file. Only the stale-cache
hypothesis explained the mismatch.

**How to apply:** for any in-browser verification of `ui/`, serve the folder through a
no-store handler (a throwaway copy lived at `runs/probes/serve_ui.py`, gitignored and
therefore not durable — recreate it if missing), and confirm the loaded script matches
disk by comparing a marker string before trusting a result. A plain page reload or
`?query=` on the page URL does not defeat it.
"}
